Right — GLI-247 was pure theater: CEO "delegated to HR Assistant" using the **CTO's agent id**, CTO posted a nice plan table, and both issues got stamped `done` with zero agents created. Handled on both fronts:

**1. The hiring is actually done now.** Six SLM-focused agents created via the API, each with a working config (groq/compound + your key, same as the execs):

| Agent | Focus |
|---|---|
| SLM Research Lead | research direction, scaling laws, distillation |
| Training Engineer | training pipelines, throughput |
| Quantization Engineer | int8/int4/fp4, size/quality benchmarks |
| Data Engineer | dataset curation and pipelines |
| Eval Engineer | benchmark harness, regression tracking |
| SLM Tech Writer | READMEs, model cards, experiment journals |

GLI-247 has a comment documenting the hires and is closed `done` — legitimately this time.

**2. Adapter v0.7.6 blocks the "plan-then-done" scam.** The tool layer now refuses `paperclip_update_issue_status: done` unless the run executed at least one substantive action (created a sub-task or agent, assigned an issue, wrote a file, or ran a command). A run that only posted comments gets an error back telling it to do the work or use `in_review`/`blocked`. Comments and plans alone can no longer close an issue.

Honest caveat: the guard is per-run heuristic — an agent that does real work in run 1 and closes in run 2 passes (correctly), and an issue whose entire job is answering a question will need `in_review` instead of `done`. That's the right trade given what these models keep pulling.
